One voice, part 1: one speaker per topic
items.text: Netra apps on the same phone recognise each other (same Netra signature only) and agree on who speaks. Each topic, like battery percent or temperature, is announced by one app only, never twice. All on the phone, offline, never between different phones.

items.title: One voice, part 2: apps can ask each other for status
items.text: An app can ask another Netra app on the same phone for information it lacks, such as battery or temperature state. Still offline and on the same phone only.

items.title: Battery and temperature check before a game
items.text: Before a KBC game starts it reads this phone's own battery and temperature. If the phone is 42 C or hotter the game is held until it cools. A TEST button on the home screen shows the reading. If the temperature is unknown the game is never blocked. Local check only; asking the other Netra apps comes later.

items.title: Festival open animations

items.title: Mic and camera switched off when the screen turns off, and where each app's data goes
items.text: Netra Privacy Guard cuts microphone and camera access when the screen turns off - this part already ships since v1.0.x. The remaining part is new: per app, which domains it contacted and the country of the destination IP, seen through the on-device DNS filter. DNS-visibility only (not full traffic or byte counts); the country is destination-IP geography, not proof of where data is stored. Needs Android 10+ for per-app naming; everything stays on the phone.

items.title: Disaster alerts, part 1: weather orange alerts (India)
items.text: Released fallback in Hub v1.4.12: the NDMA SACHET feed is checked about every 30 minutes, subject to Android delays. Severe or Extreme alerts match district, locality or state names, not coordinates. IMD alerts arrive only if present in that feed; this is not a verified IMD orange/red mapping. The original 5-minute server-driven push design is incomplete. Phone delivery is untested. The 14 Oct 8 PM target was missed; a new completion date is Unavailable until those gaps are verified.

items.title: Disaster alerts, part 2: earthquakes within about 200 km
items.text: What the app does today: a card and a check about every 30 minutes read the USGS feed for quakes of magnitude 2.5 and above within 200 km in the last 7 days, and notify about new ones. It is not an official warning, and smaller quakes in India may be missing. NDMA is not used for quakes yet. In the app since Hub v1.4.x, not yet tested on a phone.

Netra Travel Rider v1: offline push-to-talk Bluetooth intercom for riders (QR create/join with channel code, auto-play incoming voice, auto-reconnect, mute, helmet headset support, one speaker at a time, 4-6 riders, SOS alert to all, screen-off foreground service) + basic offline map (download region, own GPS position) + opt-in in-channel location sharing with last-known timestamp. Later (v1.1, early Dec): phone-to-phone map transfer, buddy direction arrow, rally point, leader/sweeper roles, breadcrumb trail, someone-left-group alert. Mesh relay and public location sharing stay undecided.

Privacy Guard: foreground-only microphone while the screen is ON - the mic works only for the app actually open on screen, not for apps sitting in the background. Level 1: instant alert naming any background app that grabs the mic, with a one-tap jump to its system permission page (works for everyone, no extras). A Level 2 with true per-app blocking was tried and removed the same day: it needed extra setup that most people would not manage, and a privacy feature people cannot understand can do more harm than good. Level 1 (alerts) is what ships.
